prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a low-speed head-on collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1087; do not mention it.)
text:
This firm represents the injured party in connection with the collision described in your file. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, or in person. Should your insured or any representative of your company wish to speak with our client, that request must come through this firm.

We ask that you disclose the bodily injury and property damage liability limits under the policy issued to your insured, together with a certified copy of the declarations page and any excess or umbrella coverage that may apply.

Our client sustained injuries in what was a low-speed head-on impact. Because the injuries and the vehicle damage are central to any claim, we request that your company preserve all evidence relating to the accident. This includes photographs, dash camera or telematics data, event data recorder downloads, repair estimates, adjuster notes, recorded statements, and any vehicle or part removed from service. Please suspend any routine destruction or salvage process until this matter is resolved.

We look forward to your prompt written confirmation of these requests.
